definitions.gloss: to go overboard; to cut loose; to get carried away; to go too far
definitions.explanation: To lose self-control and behave excessively, especially in the context of having fun or celebrating. Implies going beyond reasonable limits.

examples.japanese: ⟦{飲|の}みすぎ→飲みすぎ：22059_nomisugi⟧て{羽目|はめ}を{外|はず}した。
examples.english: I drank too much and got carried away.

examples.japanese: ⟦{久|ひさ}しぶり→久しぶり：01711_hisashiburi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{休|やす}み→休み：02266_yasumi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{羽目|はめ}を{外|はず}してしまった。
examples.english: I went overboard since it was my first day off in a long time.

examples.japanese: ⟦{楽|たの}しむ→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧、{羽目|はめ}を{外|はず}さないよう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
examples.english: It's fine to have fun, but don't go overboard, okay?

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{羽目|はめ}→羽目：11113_hame⟧ originally refers to the bit placed in a horse's mouth for control. To ⟦{外|はず}す→外す：02394_hazusu⟧ (remove) it means the horse runs wild — hence, to lose restraint.

USAGE:
Most commonly used about drinking and partying. Usually implies that the person was having fun but went too far. Can be used self-deprecatingly or as a warning to others.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {羽目|はめ}を{外|はず}しすぎる (to go way too far)
- {羽目|はめ}を{外|はず}さないよう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (so as not to go overboard)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{調子|ちょうし}→調子：03491_choushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧: to get carried away, to push one's luck — emphasis on getting overconfident
- ⟦やり→やる：02980_yaru⟧すぎる: to overdo it — more direct and general
